web.title: Hijacked Optimizely Scripts Served Card Skimmer and iOS Exploit Kits to CNN, BBC and Zoom Visitors
web.description: An attacker exploited a flaw in Optimizely Web Experimentation to plant malicious code in some of the scripts that customers' websites load from the service, Optimizely said early today.   Visitors to sites run by at least 178 organizations, including CNN, the BBC and Zoom, received the code yesterday, according to Report URI, a firm that monitors the scripts websites run.   The code was built to replace crypto wallet addresses with the attacker's own addresses and to capture card details, but the firm cannot see how many card numbers were exposed to the attacker. The vendor says it has fixed the flaw and removed the code. web.title: Six Unpatched Danfoss Refrigeration Controller Flaws Could Allow Remote Takeover Without Login
web.description: Six flaws in Danfoss AK-SM800A refrigeration controllers could let a remote attacker take over a controller without logging in, Dutch security consultancy Midnight Blue said earlier this week.   No patch is available, and the researchers say the newest firmware, version 5.4.0, does not fix the flaws.   Government cybersecurity agencies in Belgium, Ireland and Germany told operators this week to take the controllers' management interfaces off the internet.   For a controller left on the internet, updating the firmware, changing default passwords or turning on Strict mode is not enough on its own, the Belgian and Irish agencies said. Strict mode is a login protection that requires encrypted connections and session tokens, but one of the six flaws is in the gateway that enforces it.   The AK-SM800A runs a store's fridges and freezers, and maintenance firms can manage it remotely.
